the globally optimal solution for rate-fidelity packetization can be found in O(N/super 2/L/super 2/) time and that an O(NL/super 2/)-time algorithm is possible for convex rate-fidelity functions.

the problem of how to optimally allocate the available channel bandwidth to the scalable code stream so as to maximize the expected fidelity of the reconstructed signal.
the problem of finding a rate-fidelity-optimal packetization of a scalable code stream for transmission over a lossy channel.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the problem of globally optimal uneven error-protecting packetization of scalable bit streams has been resolved for a large class of erasure channel models.

the problem of rate-fidelity optimal uneven error protection for scalable source code streams can be solved optimally in O(NL/super 2/) time if either the rate-fidelity functions of the source code stream are convex or the packet loss probabilities are monotonic in the number of lost packets.

, for the first time, globally optimal solutions to rate-fidelity optimal uneven error-protecting packetization problems can be found in polynomial time, and that the time complexity is O(NL/super 2/) for convex input rate-fidelity function, and O(N/sup L/sup 2/), where L is the packet size, for the general case.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the problem of rate-fidelity optimal error protection of scalable code streams with uneven error-protection can be solved in polynomial time, with a complexity that is independent of the number of bits in the code stream.

the complexity of rate-fidelity optimal scalable packetization can be significantly reduced by making a convexity assumption on the rate-fidelily function of the scalable source code, which is often the case in practice.

for scalable video streams with uneven error-protection and convex rate-fidelity function, the complexity of finding the optimal solution can be reduced from O(N/sup3/) to O(N) with a simple modification to the algorithm.
